chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
"Lending to a believer is a gain and a hastening of goodness; if he becomes able, he repays it, and if he dies, it is counted as part of his zakat."

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer who is the recipient of the loan
key_terms.زَكَاتِهِ: his zakat, from which it is counted
key_terms.غَنِيمَةٌ: a gain or profitable benefit in spiritual terms
key_terms.قَرْضُ: a loan given to another person

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for lending money to a believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents giving a loan to a believer as a spiritually profitable act and an immediate form of goodness. It also indicates that whether the debt is repaid in life or not due to death, the lender still receives divine consideration for the act, including its being counted from his zakat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Lending to a believer is a gain and a hastening of goodness; if he becomes able to repay, he does so, and if he dies, it is counted as part of his zakat."
